item.title: Iran War Live Updates: After Month of War, Hegseth Says Iran Retains Ability to Strike
item.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth conceded that U.S.-Israeli attacks had not thwarted Iran’s missile capabilities. He said that only President Trump could decide when to end the war, which has rattled the global economy.

item.title: Europe Has a ‘Guns vs. Butter’ Problem. War in Iran Makes It Worse.
item.summary: After decades of prioritizing domestic over military spending, the continent’s leaders are trying to pivot. That is straining national budgets and could anger voters.

item.title: King Charles to Visit U.S. as Tensions Rise Between Trump and Britain
item.summary: President Trump has fired criticism at America’s longtime ally over the war in Iran, but there are hopes that the royal visit will help shore up relations.

item.title: How the U.K.’s Leader Decides Which U.S. Bombers to Let Fly Against Iran
item.summary: As the United States expands its armada of warplanes on British soil, Prime Minister Keir Starmer says he is trying to defend Britain’s interests while keeping the country out of war.

item.title: Israel Passes Law to Hang Palestinians Convicted of Deadly Attacks
item.summary: Experts say the law was written in such a way as to ensure that it was unlikely to ever apply to Jewish extremists who commit similar crimes.

item.title: For the Global Economy, ‘All Roads Lead to Higher Prices and Slower Growth’
item.summary: The effects of the war in Iran are squeezing consumers, businesses and governments around the world, raising the prices of many essential goods.

item.title: Arab World Faces ‘Profound’ Economic Crisis From Iran War, U.N. Agency Warns
item.summary: An economic simulation warned that the region’s economy could lose more than $190 billion in just one month, and that Gulf states that have often bankrolled reconstruction efforts will be less able to help.

item.title: Trump Faces a Decision on Whether to Start a Ground War in Iran
item.summary: The president wants a negotiation, but the Iranians say they are refusing until a cease-fire is declared. And while Marines and the 82nd Airborne Division offer new leverage, the risks escalate quickly.

item.title: U.S. Senators Press Taiwan to Raise Military Spending, as China Protests
item.summary: Four visiting senators urged Taiwan to break an impasse over a $40 billion budget proposal, highlighting concerns in Washington about the threat from China.

item.title: International Booker Prize Shortlist: 6 Novels With ‘Burning Humanity’
item.summary: Books by Marie NDiaye, Daniel Kehlmann and Rene Karabash are among the shortlisted titles for the major award for fiction translated into English.
